_about: Byte-cited inventory of VICEROY.EXE runtime state (DGROUP offsets) for the DOSBox Cheat Engine bridge. Every entry cites the repo doc that carries the byte-verified evidence (per CLAUDE.md prime directive). Tiers: B = byte-verified at a cited EXE site, A = oracle/runtime-confirmed, R = reconstructed gloss. 'live' fields record the 2026-08-19 in-container DOSBox 0.74-3 verification session (see README.md §Verification).

primary.note: Static section-name table; unique in VICEROY.EXE (verified against the reconstituted EXE at file 0x1FBF8 = DGROUP file base 0x1D9A0 + 0x2258) and unique in live DOSBox RAM (docs/RUNTIME_SNAPSHOT.md).

secondary.note: @ORDERS column-2 accelerator/status letters, 13 bytes. Populated by the NAMES.TXT loader at boot, so valid only once the game is past its loaders (not present in the static EXE image). Used as a confidence check, not the primary anchor.

map_notes.tile_indexing: tile byte = plane[y * map_width + x] (tile reader func_005D9C: arg2 * [0x853A] + far ptr + arg1). Record/HUD coordinates index the planes DIRECTLY — live-verified on both a generated New-World map (2026-08-19) and AMER2 (Jamestown (51,42) = land).
map_notes.terrain_byte: bits 0-4 terrain id (8..23 auto-forest, fold (id&7)|8); bit 0x20 special-terrain flag (selects id 27/28 path in func_0624E); bits 0x40/0x80 overlay bits (formats/MP_FORMAT.md).
map_notes.membase_pitfall: Emulated phys 0 is NOT necessarily the base of the DOSBox host allocation: under DOSBox 0.74-3 (Linux) the mmap region begins 0x10 bytes BEFORE phys 0, so 'region offset = phys addr' is off by 16 bytes (it silently shifts every plane read by 16 = looks like a bogus (16,1) toroidal map shift). Always derive MemBase from the BIOS Data Area signature: the unique address MB with u16[MB+0x413]==640 and populated INT 08h/21h vectors. The Lua bridge does this; a footnote for tools/runtime_snapshot.py absolute-phys claims.
map_notes.fog_bits: explored plane [0x168]: sticky bit (1 << (power+4)) per tile (spec/systems/exploration.md). Live-verified: bit 0x10 set on the England ship's tile and on newly revealed tiles after a move.
